page: Microsoft Azure D4d_v4 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the DDv4 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8272CL x86_64 processor operating at 2.6 GHz. The processor includes a 35 MB L3 cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 KB L1D cache. It supports hardware-assisted virtualization and advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512, AVX512_VNNI, and AES cryptography.

The instance is equipped with 16.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB per vCPU. It includes a bundled 154 GB local SSD for temporary storage, which is beneficial for workloads requiring low-latency scratch space. No dedicated GPU hardware is present on this server configuration.

Benchmark results indicate that the D4d_v4 delivers modest processing capabilities. In stress-ng and Passmark CPU tests, both single-core and multi-core performances fall into the bottom 25% tier. Memory bandwidth tests show weak to poor performance, with large-block read-only bandwidth measured at 22.2 GB/sec. However, single-threaded operations like gzip compression and bzip3 decompression achieve average tier results. Geekbench scores also reflect average single-core performance but weak multi-core scaling, compiling, and image processing capabilities.

From a resource density perspective, the D4d_v4 offers a balanced hardware profile suitable for entry-level general-purpose workloads. Given its modest CPU and memory bandwidth benchmarks, it is best suited for lightweight web serving, basic text processing, and development or testing environments that benefit from local SSD storage but do not require sustained high-throughput compute or memory performance.
